newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: KLASCO CARGO HANDLING UP IN 7 MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: KLASCO CARGO HANDLING UP IN 7 MONTHS.

text.p: Lithuanian state-run Klaipeda Stevedoring (KLASCO) said on Monday it handled 5.277 million tonnes of cargo in the first seven months of 1997 compared with 3.998 million tonnes in the same period in 1996.
"We handled 803,000 tonnes of cargo in July compared to 660,000 tonnes in June," finance director Algirdas Kateiva told Reuters.
He said that in July 1996 the firm handled 578,000 tonnes of cargo.
Kateiva said the increase on the turnover was due to the rising volume of metal cargo.
"During the seven months of the year we have handled more than one million tonnes more of metal cargoes than in the same period in 1996," Kateiva said.
The company said it handled 2.443 million tonnes of metal cargo in the first half of the year compared to 1.415 million tonnes in the first six month of the year.
"During the first 10 days of August we feel an acute deficit of railway carriges so it seems we might reload less cargo this month than in June," Kateiva said.
KLASCO is 90 percent state-run and is the most active loader in Klaipeda port.
The company handled 7.5 million tonnes of cargo in 1996 and reported 16.6 million litas pre-tax profit in the first half of 1997.
The government has slated the firm for privatisation and is expected to decide on the government's advisor for the selloff before the end of the month.
